name: Rodeo Drive / Special Events / Holiday Program Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday
  Program Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, June 12, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  June 12, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells, Assistant City
  Manager Ryan Gohlich, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis,
  Special Events Film Coordinator Patricia Betancourt, Police Lieutenant
  Renato Moreno

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Request from Not Today Cancer to Host “Run of the Stars” a 5k Run/Walk Sunday,
  October 6, 2024:
  a. Presentation by Patricia Betancourt:
  i. Not Today Cancer is requesting support for the 4th Annual Memorial 5K
  “Run of the Stars” event and associated permit and personnel fee waivers.
  ii. The race will not require any full street closures, the event will use
  sidewalks only.
  iii. The route will start at El Rodeo School, then go east down Elevado Ave,
  make a left on Walden Dr, then make a right on Lomitas Ave, followed by
  a right on Rodeo Dr, then a left on Elevado Ave, a right on Alpine Dr,
  another right on Carmelita Ave, a third right on Walden Dr, then turning left
  Elevado Ave and finishing at El Rodeo.
  iv. High volume crosswalks will have traffic control officers to assist
  pedestrians and vehicles.
  v. Residents along the route will be notified ten days prior to the event.
  vi. Not Today Cancer is requesting the waiving of $4,857 of Special Event
  fees, Traffic Control Officer fees, and No Parking Sign fees.
  vii. The event has already obtained a Charitable Solicitations permit for the
  event.
  viii. The proposal for the event will be brought before the full council at the July
  2nd meeting.
  b. Both Mayor Friedman and Councilmember Wells are in full support of the program.
 Highlights for June 12, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  c. Registration for the event is online and registration will cost $35 and will increase
  to $50 by race day. There will be a special kids race to encourage youth
  participation.
  d. BHUSD is in full support of and are cooperating with the event.

  3) Proposal for Rodeo Drive Holiday Décor 2024:
  a. The two Holiday Décor theme options presented by the RDC were “Merry & Bright,
  a Shopping Delight!” and “Rodeo Nights, Holiday Lights!”.
  b. The inspiration for this year’s Rodeo center median designs are vintage
  ornaments, tree toppers, icicles, and fireworks.
  c. The featured ornaments are 4’ diameter “ornaments” with an interior oversized
  accessory highlighted with LED lights, 10’ tall tree toppers, 8’ and 10’ tall colorful
  icicle swirls, 3’ tall/wide colorful vintage inspired accent ornaments, and 6’, 8’, and
  12’ tall LED customizable “fireworks”.
  d. There are four sets of Vignettes. The first is titled Pink/Green featuring the Shield
  on a tree topper as well as ornaments and fireworks. The second is titled Tree
  Topper w/ Accessory featuring swirls, ornaments, and fireworks. The third is called
  Happy Hanukah which features swirls, fireworks, and a ribbon that reads “Happy
  Hannukah”. The last Vignette is called Rodeo Nights, Holiday Lights which features
  swirls, fireworks, ornaments, and a ribbon that reads “Rodeo Nights, Holiday
  Lights”.
  e. The total estimated cost of the décor is $524,502, which is an 8% increase from
  last year.
  f. Part of the cost increase is the additional week the décor will be up since the
  lighting ceremony is on November 14th, which is a week earlier than last year. This
  is due to labor costs associated with the increased cleaning and maintenance of
  the décor as well as the increased time for equipment rentals.
  g. The cost increase for the center median holiday décor elements is due to each
  Vignette being 48’ long instead of concentrated onto 16’ elevated platforms. This
  is an additional 288’ of decorated area as compared to the 16’ platforms.
  h. The majority of the 8% increase is due to the change in décor as opposed to the
  extra week.
  i. The color palate was inspired by the colors of vintage ornaments.
  j. This item will come before the full council on June 27th.
  k. Councilmember Wells was torn over the choice of theme options and prefers a
  potential merger of the two name options. For the budget she is uncomfortable
  with the cost of the décor but is ok with sending it before the full council.
  l. For the theme options Mayor Friedman likes the “Merry and Bright” but finds the
  “a Shopping Delight” too self-serving. He is fine with either option two or a merger
  of the two that incorporates the phrase “Merry and Bright”. He is ok with the budget
  due to the explanations of the cost increases.

  4) Ci tywide Holiday Decor:
  a. The Wilshire Span refurbishment will cost $85,000.
 Highlights for June 12, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  b. The two options for the Menorah Lighting Ceremony are either Friday, December
  27th or Monday, December 30th.
  c. The removal of the lights and décor is recommended for Sunday, January 5th.
  d. The total cost for the Beverly Canon Gardens décor with the Maybourne White tree
  is $510,000. The city has only budgeted $250,000. With modifications the cost can
  be brought down to $345,000. The Maybourne has agreed to contribute $75,000,
  which leaves a $20,000 funding gap.
  e. This gap can be filled either with contingency funds or value engineering the tree
  and packages.
  f. Mayor Friedman has a problem with going over the allotted budget and directed
  staff to make what changes are necessary to bring the cost down. Councilmember
  Wells supported this decision.
  g. Options for cost savings for the projection mapping are: to reuse content instead
  of developing new shows which would save $150,000, to reuse partial content,
  which could save between $0 and $150,000 depending on how much is reused
  versus new content, only projecting onto one tower face with one set of projectors
  and one scaffolding tower which would save up to $150,000, and lastly reducing
  the runtime of the show to start after Thanksgiving instead of at the 14 th which
  would save between $50,000 to $75,000.
  h. The City is replacing the diesel generators brought to the front lawn for the
  projection mapping and for other events with electric infrastructure to reduce the
  city’s carbon footprint. This will cost $115,000.
  i. If the Projection Mapping is scrapped, staff recommends targeting investment into
  additional décor for Beverly Gardens Park on the block between Beverly and
  Rodeo.
  j. The installation of electric infrastructure to replace the diesel generators on the
  front lawn would be useful for other events such as the annual Vanity Fair event,
  and the city would be able to charge for the electricity used for the event.
  k. Mayor Friedman and Councilmemebr Wells are opposed to cutting the front lawn
  infrastructure improvements even if the Projection Mapping is scrapped.
  l. The new content for the Projection Mapping show is being done by a new local
  contractor as the contractor who designed the last two shows did not put in an offer
  to create this year’s show. The new contractor’s show is compatible with the prior
  two, which will allow for a mix and match of the three shows for the coming years.
  m. The Liaisons are against pushing the start of the Projection Mapping.
  n. Both Liaisons support the Wilshire Span light refurbishment.
  o. Mayor Friedman brought up the possibility of having the Wilshire Span lights
  switched to blue from December 11th through December 13th for the Antisemitism
  conference.
  p. December 26th is a Staff Holiday which is why the date was not chosen for the
  Menorah Lighting.
  q. The Preferred date for the Menorah Lighting is Friday, December 27th.

  5) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: June 12, 2024 / 4:30 PM
